title: Choosing the compute: request profile, cost model and effort to migrate

videos.script: Three teams ask the same question. Which compute should we use? {{three}} One runs an API that never sleeps. One runs a tool people use in office hours. One receives a batch of files at two in the morning, and nothing else all day. They should not get the same answer, and this lesson shows why. {{profile}} It starts with the traffic. You write it down as 24 numbers, one per hour, and read four things off it. The volume, the peak, the idle hours, and how long a request takes. {{program}} Then a short program reads the price sheet from lesson 1 and prices each profile four ways. EC2, Fargate, Lambda and App Runner. You will see Lambda win by a factor of nearly twenty, then lose by more than five. {{limits}} Price is half the decision. The other half is what the move costs. Disks, sessions, a fifteen-minute limit on a function, and a thirty-second limit on an API. moto accepts values past both, so this lesson reads them from the documentation. {{shop}} Last, one shop takes the whole decision, from its traffic to the numbers that would make it change its mind.
